newsitem.title: JAPAN: Philippines central bank sees no capital flight.
newsitem.headline: Philippines central bank sees no capital flight.

text.p: Capital is not fleeing the Philippines despite the recent fall in the local stock market and the peso is likely to remain stable, Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson said on Monday.
"I am confident the exchange rate will be stable," he told Reuters Financial Televsion during the Asian Development Bank annual meeting.
Singson said money was not fleeing the Philippines after the recent stock market tumble and was more likely being switched into peso fixed income assets.
"I am convinced money is not leaving the country," he said.
The central bank in the past two weeks has raised overnight interest rates and intervened in the currency market to defend the peso as share prices fell.
The stock market fall, which was triggered by worries of a property collapse, was only temporary, he said, adding that in fact the exposure of banks to the real estate sector was fairly low.
He ruled out the liklihood of any financial bailouts in the near future.

Singson repeated that the government's planned yankee bond issue, delayed last month, would only be when the market conditions were right, but declined specify what sort of spread the government was seeking.
